content:
incident-bot: Pager: HIGH — customer Ceres Technologies (private VPC) is seeing intermittent 502s from valencia-prod. Affects inference endpoints on Dedicated pool 'valencia-prod'. NLB target group healthchecks flapping. Links: runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/vpc-egress-nlb

oncall-jess: I’m on it. tagging net and sre. what’s the customer impact right now?

account-liz: Customer reports ~20% of requests returning 502s over the last 12m. Large batch jobs failing; CSM flagged as P1. Ceres wants ETA for mitigation.

net-raj: quick snapshot: NLB (nlb-valencia-a) shows unhealthy targets in TG-0a1b2c. HealthCheckPath = /healthz, 10s interval. Logs show TCP handshake success but HTTP health check returns 502 from target. I can tail the targets:```
# tail -n 50 /var/log/nginx/access.log | grep healthz
10.1.4.12 - - [15/Mar/2026:09:12:01 +0000] "GET /healthz HTTP/1.1" 502 162 "-" "ELB-HealthChecker/2.0"
10.1.4.15 - - [15/Mar/2026:09:12:11 +0000] "GET /healthz HTTP/1.1" 502 162 "-" "ELB-HealthChecker/2.0"
```

eng-tom: recent deploy? deploy-bot: `deploy-bot: deploy complete valencia-service @ 2026-03-15T09:08:03Z (rev: a1f3c4)`

sre-olivia: good catch. If the app is returning 502 for the health check but TCP OK, could be a dependency (auth, db) flapping. We should isolate tenant traffic to avoid noisy neighbor and failover to valencia-b. Two parallel actions: 1) short DNS weight shift to valencia-b (weighted route53) 2) isolate suspected instance(s) by adding SG deny for external inference pool to redirect test traffic to internal debug proxy.

oncall-jess: agree. net-raj, can you prepare the route53 change? I'll get sign-off from account-liz for customer comms before doing DNS move.

net-raj: prepping change batch. Proposed: change weight from nlb-valencia-a (weight 80) -> nlb-valencia-b (weight 20) to 20/80. Route53 change JSON ready:```
{
  "Comment": "weighted shift for emergency failover",
  "Changes": [
    {
      "Action": "UPSERT",
      "ResourceRecordSet": {
        "Name": "valencia.prod.redwood.internal.",
        "Type": "A",
        "SetIdentifier": "nlb-valencia-b",
        "Weight": 80,
        "AliasTarget": { "HostedZoneId": "ZNLB..", "DNSName": "nlb-valencia-b" }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

account-liz: Ceres is already on the line with CS. We can do a partial weight shift (20%). Tell them we're routing a portion of traffic to the backup pool for safety. cs-ana, want me to send a one-line to customer?

cs-ana: yes please. Send: "We're routing a portion of traffic to a backup pool to reduce errors while we triage. No action needed on your side. We'll update in 10m"

oncall-jess: go ahead with DNS weight shift. Net-raj, post the change-id when submitted.

net-raj: running:
`aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z12345 --change-batch file://weight-shift.json`
Change submitted: C1234567890
ETA propagation ~ 60s. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

deploy-bot: Deploy detection: recent config change in valencia-service: `enable_outbound_conn_pool=true` bumped at rev a1f3c4 — might be related.

eng-tom: that config could surface upstream timeout issues. If the app mutated how it handles backend retries, healthcheck responses could be affected. Recommend temporarily reverting that flag on a small set of instances. net-raj can we mark two instances to drain from nlb-a?

net-raj: I can set the targets to drained state:```
aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:tg/TG-0a1b2c --targets Id=10.1.4.12 Id=10.1.4.15
```
Deregister in flight.

sre-olivia: Also spin up debug proxy on 10.1.9.9 and update security group to only allow healthchecks from NLB source. `aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-abc --protocol tcp --port 8080 --cidr 10.0.0.0/8` then curl the internal path.

oncall-jess: Done with the weight change — seeing decrease in 502s in synthetic checks. Cloudwatch: 502 rate down from 18% -> 6% in 90s.

account-liz: passing update to Ceres: "We've routed 60% traffic to backup pool and removed two suspect instances from primary. Error rate improving; continuing triage."

cs-ana: customer responded: "Thanks — please advise when fully resolved." They asked if there was a deploy. I confirmed there was a config flip earlier.

eng-tom: plan: 1) keep weighted shift for 30m, 2) run targeted rollback of the flag on a small subset (canary), 3) if canary passes, roll forward full rollback or patch. Who owns rollback?

oncall-jess: eng-tom do the canary rollback. net-raj continue to watch NLB targets. Sre-olivia please confirm no other tenants impacted.

net-raj: TG health back to normal on most targets. still one host flapping but it's drained. no cross-tenant traffic observed.

sre-olivia: Verified via VPC flow logs and our tenant tagging that only Ceres IPs were impacted. No other customers affected.

eng-tom: Canary rollback applied to 2 instances (rev a1f3c4 -> a1f3c3). Canaries show stable healthchecks and successful inference requests.

oncall-jess: great. reduce weighted shift back to 90/10 in 5m, then 100/0 once metrics stable for 10m. Net-raj, are you ready?

net-raj: lowering weight now. Change-id: C1234567891. New weights 90/10.

oncall-jess: Metrics: 502 rate 1.2% now, latency normal. Rolling back full weight to primary in 8m unless new regressions.

account-liz: Customer update: sent. They acknowledged and asked for postmortem details.

incident-bot: Incident marked mitigated -> partial rollback + config rollback canary succeeded. Owner required for postmortem: suggested owner eng-tom. Runbook step: triage->isolate->rollback.

eng-tom: I’ll own postmortem. Drafting timeline + root cause: config flag caused backend retries to surface auth timeouts which returned 502 to healthcheck path.

oncall-jess: closing pager for now. leaving notes and tagging for postmortem. :white_check_mark:
